summary: Frontend constructs OpenAI-shaped ToolCall from flat backend WS events; types.ts WSServerMessage changed to match backend's flat shape, duplicating protocol knowledge in two frontend files
failure_scenario: Backend changes tool_call payload (e.g., adds 'type' field) -> both types.ts and client.ts must be updated in sync, or deserialization silently drops fields / breaks type checking. Single source of truth should live in backend schemas.py with codegen or shared package.

summary: Backend chat.py emits flat WS events (type='tool_call', tool_name, arguments, tool_call_id) but OpenAI protocol expects nested structure; frontend compensates in client.ts:251-258 by manually constructing nested ToolCall
failure_scenario: If backend switches to OpenAI-compatible WS protocol (nested tool_calls array), frontend's manual constructor breaks silently (toolCall.function.name becomes undefined). Protocol divergence creates drift risk; backend should emit canonical OpenAI shape.

summary: Monaco editors in DeckEditor, DeckBuilder, and LinterPanel hardcoded to theme='vs-dark'/'opm-dark'; ThemeApplier in App.tsx only sets data-theme on document.documentElement but Monaco doesn't read CSS variables
failure_scenario: User switches to light mode via SettingsPanel -> data-theme='light' on <html> -> CSS variables flip to light palette, but all Monaco editors remain hardcoded dark ('vs-dark') creating dark editor islands in light UI. Fix requires useEditorTheme hook reading useTheme() from UI store.

summary: Plotly charts rendered via Plotly.newPlot with no template/theme config; Plotly defaults to white background which clashes with dark theme CSS variables
failure_scenario: Dark mode enabled -> plot backgrounds stay white, axis labels use dark text on dark container background = unreadable charts. Plotly needs layout.template='plotly_dark' or explicit paper_bgcolor/plot_bgcolor from CSS vars via useTheme hook.

summary: SPAStaticFiles.get_response catches ALL 404s (line 26) including /assets/*.js 404s from typos or missing build artifacts; returns index.html with 200 OK -> browser parses HTML as JS -> cryptic 'Unexpected token <' console error
failure_scenario: User typos <script src='/assets/main.js'> vs actual /assets/main-xyz.js -> 404 -> SPA fallback serves index.html -> browser executes HTML as JS -> blank screen with confusing error. Fix: only fallback for paths without file extension OR with Accept: text/html header.

summary: SimulationRunner uses currentJob from localStorage-persisted zustand store but has no mount effect to reconcile with backend; backend session_store is in-memory and clears on restart
failure_scenario: User runs simulation -> job stored in localStorage as 'running' -> backend restarts (deploy, crash) -> in-memory job_store cleared -> user revisits /simulator -> UI shows stale 'Running' job forever (no 404 check on mount). ResultsViewer.tsx:76-82 has partial reconciliation but only triggers on status change, not on mount.

summary: decks.py writes to tempfile.mkdtemp() relying on paths.py allowlist including system temp dir; no test enforces this coupling - paths.py hardening could silently break /api/decks
failure_scenario: Future paths.py change removes tempfile.gettempdir() from allowed roots (e.g., to tighten sandbox) -> saveDeck() raises ValueError 'Path outside allowed roots' -> /api/decks 500s -> DeckBuilder 'Use Last Built Deck' and LinterPanel 'Lint Deck' both break silently. No test guards this dependency.

summary: paths.py get_allowed_roots() unconditionally adds system temp dir (line 29) as allowlist root for smoke tests; this widens attack surface and couples API routes to temp directory behavior
failure_scenario: If temp directory permissions change or sandbox restricts access, deck saving/linting fails non-deterministically. Better: explicit configured decks_dir in settings with test that validates path resolution, rather than implicit tempdir allowlist.
